Day 08 of 100 · AWS Networking Foundations

Route Tables

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityAWS Networking FoundationsTopic confirmed · archive artifact pending
Archive artifact still required.

User-confirmed topic; original Day 8 artifact pending.

The topic is now confirmed by the project owner, so the technical article is populated. The canonical ledger status is not promoted until the original published artifact is recovered.

Route tables decide where packets leaving a subnet are sent by matching destination prefixes to targets such as local VPC routing, gateways or network connections.

Architecture / mental model

packet destination → longest-prefix route match → target (local / IGW / NAT / endpoint / TGW / peering)

How it works

Every VPC has routing logic, including a local route that enables communication inside the VPC CIDR. Subnets are explicitly or implicitly associated with route tables.

A route contains a destination prefix and a target. AWS uses the most specific matching destination route, so a narrow route can override a broad default route such as `0.0.0.0/0`.

Public/private behavior emerges from these routes. A public subnet usually has a default route to an Internet Gateway, while a private IPv4 subnet may send default outbound traffic toward a NAT Gateway.

Hands-on reference

aws ec2 describe-route-tables --query 'RouteTables[].[RouteTableId,VpcId,Associations,Routes]'

Verification

Take one instance destination, determine the source subnet's associated route table and manually identify which route should win. Then confirm with a real connectivity test.

Field note / gotcha

Editing the VPC's main route table may affect every subnet that relies on its implicit association. Check associations before treating a route change as local.

Security considerations

Routes create reachability. Do not add broad peering/TGW/internet paths without matching access controls and an explicit reason for the new trust path.

What I learned

When a packet cannot leave a subnet, the route table is one of the first places where intent becomes observable.
